name: Taking payment
summary: Subscriptions through Stripe, with payment messages proved genuine before they are believed and never counted twice.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — its Stripe integration, in particular verifying the webhook signature against the raw body and recording every event id before acting on it
provenance.changes: Reduced to subscriptions and reshaped for Next.js route handlers. The idempotency table and the raw-body handling are kept as they are, because both are the difference between a working integration and one that charges people twice.

env.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
env.description: Your Stripe key. Use a test key until you are ready to take real money.
env.obtainFrom: your Stripe dashboard, under Developers → API keys

env.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.description: The signing secret for the webhook. Without it, anyone could tell your app a payment succeeded.
env.obtainFrom: your Stripe dashboard, under Developers → Webhooks

env.name: STRIPE_PRICE_ID
env.description: Which plan people are subscribing to.

extensionPoints.description: Your plans and what each one includes.

postInstall: Create a Stripe account and a product with a recurring price.
Add a webhook endpoint in Stripe pointing at /api/billing/webhook, and copy its signing secret into your .env file.
Take one payment with a test card and check the subscription appears. Nothing here is proven until you have.
limitations: Not run against a live Stripe account here. The signature check and the double-charge protection are tested with Stripe's own test helpers; the money has never moved.
One plan at a time. No usage billing, no metered pricing, no proration handling beyond what Stripe does itself.
Tax and invoicing are left to Stripe. Whether that satisfies your local rules is a question for an accountant, not this component.
